title: Beta-blocker therapy and symptoms of depression, fatigue, and sexual dysfunction
authors: Ko DT, Hebert PR, Coffey CS, Sedrakyan A, Curtis JP, Krumholz HM
population: 15 randomised placebo-controlled, non-crossover trials with at least 100 patients in myocardial infarction, heart failure or hypertension that reported depressive symptoms, fatigue or sexual dysfunction; MEDLINE 1966 to 2001, English language
funder: not read: the publisher page refused access and the archived copy holds no article text.
result: In trials involving more than 35,000 subjects, beta-blockers did not significantly raise the annual risk of reported depressive symptoms (6 per 1000 patients, 95% CI -7 to 19). They raised reported fatigue by 18 per 1000 patients a year (5 to 30), one additional report per 57 patients treated for a year, and reported sexual dysfunction by 5 per 1000 a year (2 to 8), one per 199. Risks did not differ by lipid solubility; fatigue was significantly more frequent with early-generation than late-generation beta-blockers (P = 0.04). Adverse events were abstracted from trial reports.
